summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and recent airway surgery was readmitted due to increased sputum production and throat pain, following a recent discharge with MRSA-positive sputum culture. She reported difficulty swallowing and persistent pain despite opioid use, along with dizziness and chills but no fever or respiratory distress. A chest X-ray showed no acute process, and an endoscopic tracheal inspection revealed inflammation without obstruction or pus. She was treated with a change in antibiotics to cover MRSA safely, given her allergies, and evaluated for chronic pain and medication-related rash. Pain management and mental health support were initiated. She improved clinically, resumed oral intake, and was discharged with follow-up arranged with pulmonology, ENT, and pain services.
